fixed: The writing on the Copycat's paddle was back to front, because he faces left. Writing on a thing held in a hand now reads the right way round whichever way its holder faces.

The price tag on the dollar was cut off by the edge of the picture in the closer shots. The tag is now shown only in the wide shots and in the shots of the podium alone; the closer shots say the bid on a label or on the paddle.
The Cheat held the dollar out past the edge of the picture. He now holds it up beside his head.
An arrow that said PAID $1.80 ran across the Copycat's face. It is a label at the top of the picture now.
The Copycat's thought bubble sat on his beanie. A bubble now clears a hat, and his sum is shown in a wide shot, where there is room over his head.
Going into his close-up the Copycat's bowed head lurched across the picture for a frame. He stands upright from the shot before.
You pulled a frightened grimace when lowering your hand. It is a doubtful look now.
The shots of the podium alone slid off to one side. The dollar and the gavel now stand evenly about its middle and the camera holds still.
notes: New opening, asked for by Biku on 2026-10-11: the narrator asks 'Would you bid a nickel for a dollar bill?' in the first 2.5 seconds, and the same words stand big over the dollar on the podium, the last line in gold. The caption under them says the same words, as on every shot.

Then 'Two bidders said yes. Watch what it cost them.' over the Cheat raising his paddle and the Copycat raising his a beat later. 'Sold.' follows at 6.5 seconds; everything from there on is the first version, 6.25 seconds later.
Every line of the first version is spoken exactly as before (the length of none changed by more than a hundredth of a second).
There is still no title card: the question is the opening.
The auctioneer is a gloved hand that comes up from behind the podium. A little dark sleeve shows below the glove when the gavel is raised.
The paddles say 5 cents and 10 cents for the first two bids and BID after that; the later bids are on a label at the top and on the tag on the dollar.
The Cheat's and the Copycat's sums are thought bubbles over their heads while they say them.
The light turns red on a plain cut as the Cheat reasons his way past one dollar. That is meant.

In the wide shots the two bidders and the podium are in the upper half of the tall picture with the floor under them; shots of one person are much bigger, with the caption over the legs and, twice, over the hand holding a lowered paddle. No caption is over a face.
Several shots are quick (about a second): the gavel, 'Rewind.', 'So who won?', 'Five cents.' They are single short lines of his script.
The caption 'Me.' is on screen for a blink before 'Obviously.' takes its place.
There is no music until the light turns red; before that a room murmur, the gavel, a whoosh on the rewind and a tap for each paddle. The clock ticks from the red light on. Sound is for Biku's ears.
The voices of the Cheat and the Copycat are option 1 of the three test voices; Biku has not picked yet.
